newsitem.title: GERMANY: BHF Bank ups Bankgesellschaft to "buy".
newsitem.headline: BHF Bank ups Bankgesellschaft to "buy".

text.p: BHF Bank AG said on Monday it had raised its recommendation for shares on Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG to "Buy" from "Hold" after the Berlin bank on Friday said it was setting aside 2.2 billion marks in a one-off measure to cover credit risks.
BHF Bank analyst Dieter Hein said Bankgesellschaft shares were undervalued and had potential to rise to 30 marks in the short term and 35 marks in the medium term.
The shares were quoted at 27.25 marks at 1025 GMT, up two marks or 7.9 percent from Friday's close.
Hein said the charge was made to put Bankgesellschaft's house in order and would lead to a two mark loss per share for 1996, after an earlier forecast of a 1.60 mark profit.
But he said he had raised his forecast for 1997 earnings per share to 3.20 marks from 2.30 marks and expected a rise to 3.40 marks for 1998.
Hein said that based on Friday's closing share price and earnings projections for 1998, Bankgesellschaft had a price-earnings ratio of 7.4, well below the banking sector average of 13.

Bankgesellschaft, 56.8 percent owned by the state of Berlin, said the provision was aimed at giving the bank a clean slate for the future and covered risks in the bank's overall credit portfolio given the difficult economic situation in Berlin and east Germany.
Its chief executives, Wolfgang Steinriede and Hubertus Moser, announced on Friday they would resign from the management board at the end of December.

Wolfgang Rupf, who joined Bankgesellschaft's management board on November 1, will replace them as sole chief executive on January 1 next year. He had been scheduled to take over as chief executive later in the year.
